title: Quant metadata scale mismatch — EOS drift review
body:
Summary:

On 2024-11-13 at ~17:42 UTC we observed a gradual increase in customer-facing short responses and truncated outputs for the hosted API route using model 'open-redwood-40b-q4' after a staged model weight swap. The canary suite did not surface the problem — overall token latency and error rates remained nominal. A manual investigation revealed that a subset of weight shards had quantization metadata (per-block scale factors) written in an older format: a mismatch in scale endianness/ordering for two shard files. That produced a consistent attenuation of logits for tokens beyond a certain byte-offset and increased probability mass on the EOS token for many prompts, causing early termination (semantic truncation).

Impact:
- Affected a single model variant in the hosted catalog (open-redwood-40b-q4) in region us-west-2.
- Estimated 1.7% of generation requests showed premature EOS within first 40 tokens during the 3-hour window.
- Customer reports: 8 support tickets flagged hallucinations/truncated answers; one internal integration test failure triggered an alert.
- No increased 5xxs or infra capacity issues; CPU/GPU utilization unchanged.

Why canary missed it:
- Canary prompt set used short prompt templates (< 20 tokens) and did not include boundary-case tokens that reveal EOS-propensity.
- The canary compares aggregate perplexity and top-1 token distributions but not EOS-specific rate on longer prompts.
- The bad shards were from a late-stage incremental quant job that wasn't included in the canary bucket due to a filename pattern mismatch.

Timeline (high level):
- 2024-11-13 16:30 UTC: Incremental weight swap rollout begins (staged by shard).
- 2024-11-13 17:38 UTC: First customer support ticket mentioning "answers cut off" (low severity).
- 2024-11-13 17:42 UTC: Aggregated analytics show EOS rate on route model_open_redwood_40b_q4 rising above baseline.
- 2024-11-13 17:45 UTC: Oncall paged; SRE starts investigation.
- 2024-11-13 18:10 UTC: Reproduce locally with full prompt set, observe EOS spike.
- 2024-11-13 18:35 UTC: Identify shard filename pattern and quant metadata mismatch.
- 2024-11-13 19:05 UTC: Rollback of staged shards to previous weight set initiated.
- 2024-11-13 19:20 UTC: EOS rates return to baseline; customer tickets triaged.

Reproduction notes (commands used during triage):
- Query (replay): curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"open-redwood-40b-q4","prompt":"{{long-test-prompt}}","max_tokens":80}' | jq -r '.choices[0].text'
- Compare logits & EOS prob (dev node): python tools/inspect_logits.py --model-path /weights/open-redwood-40b-q4/staged --prompt-file tests/long_prompts.txt --dump-eos-probs /tmp/eos_probs.csv
- Inspect shard metadata: hexdump -C shard-003.quant.meta | head -n 40
- Diff quant metadata: python -c 'import json;print(set(json.load(open("shard-003.meta")))-set(json.load(open("shard-003.correct.meta"))))'

Key artifacts found:
- Two shard metadata files (shard-003.meta, shard-007.meta) had scale arrays serialized in little-endian vs expected big-endian ordering.
- The quantization pipeline (quant-optimizer v1.4.2) introduced a conditional write path when running with --fast-metadata which skipped a byte-order normalization step for shards above index 250.
- Canary release tooling filters (deploy-canary.py) excluded 'staged-*' filenames; the incremental job wrote to 'staged-idx-...'.

Root cause (RCA) hypothesis:
- A production quantization job ran with --fast-metadata to shorten write time for a large model. For performance reasons, the library used native struct.pack/array writes which on some hosts produced little-endian ordering. The runtime loader assumes a canonical big-endian order and performs no validation. When a subset of shards were written with the different ordering, the per-block scale factors used in dequantization were applied incorrectly, attenuating logits for tokens mapped to weights in those blocks. For many prompts this increased the relative probability of the EOS token, especially when the model produced long-tail tokens.

Why this is subtle:
- The numeric difference after dequantization was small magnitude but enough to change argmax for borderline tokens.
- Standard unit tests check reconstruction MSE but do not check downstream token-level distribution shifts or EOS rate.
- The issue only affects shards with block-offsets that map to commonly-used token embeddings for certain prompt styles, so not every prompt was impacted.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Rolled back staged shards to previous weight set within ~30 minutes of detection.
- Temporarily paused incremental quant jobs (safeguard toggle engaged).
- Expanded canary prompt set to include longer prompts with edge token patterns and added EOS-rate checks to the canary alert rules.

Suggested long-term fixes (action items):
- Fix quant-optimizer: always write canonical metadata ordering and add checksum + version header in metadata files. (Owner: Diego Rivera, PR #421).
- Add binary metadata validation step in serving runtime: on load, validate metadata header magic + checksum; fail-open to previous weights when validation fails. (Owner: Jordan Kim).
- Update canary test suite: include long prompt bank, introduce EOS-rate as a metric, and add automated A/B diff of token-level distributions and nucleus prob mass. (Owner: Aisha Patel).
- Deployment pipeline: prevent staged-* artifacts from being excluded from canary — canonicalize naming and include a quick verification step that new files are actually present in canary buckets. (Owner: platform-eng).
- Add a synthetic regression test: run small set of prompts through quantized vs float baseline and assert EOS delta < 0.5% and top-k KL divergence threshold. (Owner: applied-ml).

Runbook draft (for similar future incidents):
- 1) Triage: check model variant and region. Query model telemetry: eos_rate, avg_length, top1-token-shift across recent 15m window.
- 2) Reproduce: run long prompt bank against the staged variant in a dev cluster; dump token logits and eos prob.
- 3) Check artifact diffs: list weight files, check metadata checksums and sizes (ls -lh, sha256sum), hexdump first 64 bytes of .meta files.
- 4) If metadata mismatch suspected: immediately pin serving to previous version (rollback) and stop new artifact ingestion.
- 5) Notify: escalate to quant-optimizer and serving-runtime owners; open incident ticket SRE-9876 and add affected customers.
- 6) Post-rollback: run canary expanded suite for 2h; only proceed with re-rollout after passing EOS and distribution checks.

Operational notes and gotchas discovered:
- Some hosts in the quant pipeline run older libc versions where struct packing behaves differently for native-endian quick paths. Production packaging needs to standardize the build environment (we package quant-optimizer as a wheel but system-level GLIBC drift still matters for native extensions).
- Filename patterns: our canary tooling uses glob patterns that silently ignore unrecognized prefixes; the deploy flow must fail if artifact counts don't match expectation.
- Observability: EOS rate was visible only in token-level telemetry (not in generic generation success rate), so make token-level metrics higher fidelity and surfaced in the ops dashboard.

Customer communications (snippet for support):
- "We identified a subtle quantization metadata issue that briefly increased short/truncated answers for a small number of requests on one hosted model variant. We rolled back the affected weights and have deployed fixes to the packaging and verification pipelines; your integrations should be unaffected going forward."

Open action list (short):
- [ ] PR to quant-optimizer to add canonical metadata header + tests (Diego) — target 2024-11-20
- [ ] Runtime metadata validation + failover path (Jordan) — target 2024-12-01
- [ ] Expand canary test bank + EOS checks (Aisha) — target 2024-12-05
- [ ] Incident postmortem writeup with timelines and customer list (SRE lead) — target 2024-11-21
- [ ] Harden deployment artifact verification: fail deploy if artifact counts differ (platform-eng) — target 2024-11-25

Appendix (excerpts):
- Log excerpt: 2024-11-13T17:42:05Z ROUTE=model_open_redwood_40b_q4 eos_rate=0.082 baseline=0.012 delta=+0.07
- hexdump snippet (shard-003.meta):
00000000  52 45 44 57 4f 4f 44 2d  4d 45 54 41 00 01 00 00  |REDWOOD-META....|
00000010  00 00 00 02 3f 80 00 00 3f 40 00 00 3e 80 00 00  |....?.?..?@..?...|
- dev reproduction: observed mean(EOS_prob) staging=0.081, baseline=0.012 for long_prompts.txt set (n=120)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a draft RCA focused on tactical fixes and a runbook. Looking for feedback on: coverage of canary tests (are we overfitting prompts?), whether to add enforced metadata schema to artifact registry, and whether we should introduce a pre-deploy metadata validation CI gate.

Slack channels and threads referenced:
- #sre-incidents (thread: quant-eos-2024-11-13)",
